AdminCancelIn.description: An admin cancel takes a reason - it lands in the audit row the owner can be answered with.
AdminCancelIn.title: AdminCancelIn

AdminEventsOut.description:
One page of the task's durable record - raw wire payloads, exactly as the stream framed
them, so the web's replay reducer folds them unchanged. `next_since` is the last seq, or
null when the page came back short (the history is drained).
AdminEventsOut.title: AdminEventsOut

AdminUserDetailOut.description: The one-user view: the list row plus the operational facts worth a second query.
AdminUserDetailOut.title: AdminUserDetailOut

ApiKeyCreatedOut.description: Creation, and only creation, carries the plaintext - once.
ApiKeyCreatedOut.title: ApiKeyCreatedOut

ApiKeyOut.description: A key, as listed. Note what is absent: the key.
ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut

AppFinishIn.description: The app back from the browser: the one-time code the callback handed it, and its secret.
AppFinishIn.title: AppFinishIn

AppSignInIn.description:
The phone app starting an OAuth sign-in it will finish itself (RFC 8252): the S256 hash of
a secret only it holds, and which app build it is - the callback sends the browser back to
that app's scheme, picked from a fixed list.
AppSignInIn.title: AppSignInIn

ArtifactOut.description:
An artifact, with its provenance chain.

`provenance` is the manifest entry, verbatim: who made it, with which model, from which
sources, pinned to which skill versions. It is the chain that makes a claim *checkable* -
without it, a download is a file somebody swears is right.
ArtifactOut.title: ArtifactOut

AuthorizeIn.description: Optional: the web sends no body.
AuthorizeIn.title: AuthorizeIn

BotAccessOut.description: The access tab's payload - the connector half; tools/skills/ask ride BotOut.
BotAccessOut.title: BotAccessOut

BotCreateIn.description:
Creating a bot (POST) carries its name in the body; a push to an existing one (PUT) takes
the name from the path. `project_id` is set once, at birth - a bot does not move between
scopes, because its name is only unique within one.
BotCreateIn.title: BotCreateIn

BotFaceIn.description:
The face PATCH - the projects wire grammar exactly: optional values plus explicit clear
flags, because a PATCH cannot say null and "leave it alone" with one field.
BotFaceIn.title: BotFaceIn

BotJobOut.description:
A 202: the authoring work was enqueued on the worker (Rule 5 keeps model
calls out of the API process). The caller polls the bot itself: a new version appears
(draft) or `eval_status` changes (test).
BotJobOut.title: BotJobOut

BotPinOut.description:
One bot on the task's roster override: the name, and the version the pin
resolved to (None = the head at plan time).
BotPinOut.title: BotPinOut

BotPushIn.description:
An author pushing an edited bot. Either the raw `BOT.md` (the CLI) or the fields (the web).

`bot_md` wins when both are present: a file the author typed is more authoritative than a
form the client assembled from it.
BotPushIn.title: BotPushIn

BotStatsOut.description: The stats strip. Money rides as strings, the ledger's wire convention.
BotStatsOut.title: BotStatsOut

Budget.description: A ceiling. `None` means unbounded - which is a decision, not an omission.
Budget.title: Budget

BudgetFigures.description:
The money behind a "Budget reached" gate, as the Bursar saw it when the gate opened: the
ceiling it hit, what that ceiling had spent, and the coming wave's estimate when the wave
projection opened it (0 when the spend alone reached the ceiling). A raise that resumes the
wave clears `max(ceiling_usd, spent_usd + projected_usd)`.

The run guard reads the same shape live (`TaskDeps.spend`, `ai/rules/budget.reached`).
`exhausted`: the workspace has spent its allowance (ADR-103), which stops the task whatever its
ceiling - 0 when it has none. An "allowance spent" gate wears it with zero dollars: the floor it
hit is the workspace's allowance.
BudgetFigures.title: BudgetFigures

CatalogEntryOut.description:
One known provider from the data catalog. `keywords` ship so the composer's
suggestion chip can run the same word-boundary grammar client-side, at zero latency.
CatalogEntryOut.title: CatalogEntryOut

ChannelMintOut.description: Creation and rotation answer with the raw token ONCE - the ck_ ceremony.
ChannelMintOut.title: ChannelMintOut

ChatActivity.description:
A tool the reply is using, as it happens - the web's quiet "searching…" line. Labels
follow the journal's redaction posture (locators, never content).
ChatActivity.title: ChatActivity

ChatDelta.description: Markdown, append-only - never a retro-edit of what already streamed.
ChatDelta.title: ChatDelta

ChatEnd.description: Terminates in the durable bot row carrying the same markdown in full.
ChatEnd.title: ChatEnd

ChatStreamOut.description:
The conversation stream's frames, declared so the frozen contract carries
their shapes: an SSE `message` event is a `MessageOut` row (`id: seq`); `chat.start`,
`chat.delta`, `chat.activity`, `chat.end` are the reply's ephemeral frames (no id). This
model exists for the OpenAPI export - no route ever returns it as a body.
ChatStreamOut.title: ChatStreamOut

CheckOut.description:
One deterministic assertion, and what it found. `expected`/`actual` are the whole point:
*"numbers:grounded failed"* is a shrug; *"9.9 is not in any source"* is a fix.
CheckOut.title: CheckOut

CodeFileOut.description: One file in a code archive. `text` is present only for small UTF-8 members.
CodeFileOut.title: CodeFileOut

ConnectorConnectIn.description:
One-click connect: a catalog entry by slug, or a custom server by URL -
exactly one. Create + begin-authorization in one round trip.
ConnectorConnectIn.title: ConnectorConnectIn

ConnectorOut.description: A connector, as listed. The credential is exactly what is not here.
ConnectorOut.title: ConnectorOut

ConnectorStatus.description:
The row's lifecycle. `pending_auth` = created, awaiting the OAuth dance; `authorizing` =
a flow is in flight (state minted, browser out); `live` = probed and usable; `needs_reauth`
= tokens died (refresh failed or a mount saw 401); `error` = the server itself refused the
probe; `disabled` = the owner switched it off without forgetting it.
ConnectorStatus.title: ConnectorStatus

ConnectorUpdateIn.description: Rename, or flip the intent-attach dial - at least one field.
ConnectorUpdateIn.title: ConnectorUpdateIn

Criteria.title: Criteria

DocBlockOut.description: One extracted document block: a styled line (`style` ∈ h1|h2|h3|li|p) OR a table.
DocBlockOut.title: DocBlockOut

DownloadOut.description: A presigned link, signed for the public endpoint - never an internal hostname.
DownloadOut.title: DownloadOut

EmailInboundIn.description:
The ONE generic inbound-parse shape - Postmark, Mailgun, and SES-to-SNS
can all be adapted to POST this; the provider is operator infrastructure, like the
storage endpoint. `from` is spelled with an alias: a reserved word is not a wire choice.
EmailInboundIn.title: EmailInboundIn

FeedbackIn.description:
The thumbs. One press, one durable `task.feedback` frame; the newest is the
turn's current mood. Never machine state - grading an answer moves nothing.
FeedbackIn.title: FeedbackIn

FireOut.description: A 202 whatever was decided: a refused fire is a RESULT wearing its journaled reason.
FireOut.title: FireOut

FireTokenOut.description: Shown ONCE (the ck_ ceremony). Rotation supersedes; revocation closes the door.
FireTokenOut.title: FireTokenOut

FollowUpIn.description:
A follow-up **continues the SAME task** - the thread is the task: the message
becomes the next turn on the same row, same record, same stream, with the whole
conversation in the agent's hands. Never a new task; `fork` is the branching action.

It still takes the fresh-turn dials: new attachments append (a filename may not shadow an
earlier turn's), skills merge, budget/models/deliverable update when given. `project_id` and
`mode` are thread-DNA - inherited, never chosen. A live task refuses with 409 ("steer it
instead"); the client_token makes a replayed send gesture return the same turn, never two.
FollowUpIn.title: FollowUpIn

ForkIn.description:
One-click fork - THE branching action: a NEW task on the parent's thread that
carries the whole conversation and the parent's dials (budget, seats, deliverable, skill
pins), born HELD: it sits with a composer until the first directive launches it. No goal,
no dials of its own - only the duplicate-guardrail token rides along, and, for a fork of a task
on the device, the folder it works in (it never copies the parent's).
ForkIn.title: ForkIn

FrameDriverName.description:
Who makes a Machine's frames: the worker's `frame_driver` setting, or a task's own
(`tasks.machine_driver`). `conf` sits beside `schemas` and spells these as plain strings.
FrameDriverName.title: FrameDriverName

GateAction.description: The three actions, verbatim from MCP elicitation.
GateAction.title: GateAction

content.description: answers by question id (q1, q2, …). On decline, the answers given stand and every other question takes its default. Ignored for cancel.
content.title: Content

version.description: Deployed release: the pinned git sha, or 'dev'
version.title: Version

worker.description: Worker pulse: ok | never | unknown | stale <n>s
worker.title: Worker

InboundAcceptedOut.description:
202 for every accepted OR refused line (a refusal is a row wearing its reason): where it
landed, the verdict the door gave, and the task if one started.
InboundAcceptedOut.title: InboundAcceptedOut

InboxItemOut.description:
One notification.

`task_id` is the point of the whole thing. **An inbox item you cannot act on from is just noise
with a timestamp** - so every item that is *about* something carries the id of that thing,
and the next command is always obvious: `prismoid tasks show $TASK_ID`.
InboxItemOut.title: InboxItemOut

InboxTaskReadOut.description:
What opening a task did to the caller's inbox: how many of their items about it it read,
and how many of theirs stay unread anywhere (the badge). A client refreshes only when
`marked` moved.
InboxTaskReadOut.title: InboxTaskReadOut

LabelIn.description: Name (or un-name) a revision. Null clears; the operation trims and caps.
LabelIn.title: LabelIn

MeOut.description:
`/v1/auth/me` only - the caller's own profile plus their own admin standing, so the web
can gate the Admin nav entry instead of 403-probing. Deliberately NOT on the general
`UserOut`: whether someone else holds the keys is the operator's business, not a peer's.
`workspace` is the workspace this credential is working in, with the caller's role there
(ADR-061) - null once every membership is gone, when the person may only list, create or
join workspaces.
MeOut.title: MeOut

email.description: the user to share with, by email (§6)
email.title: Email

MemoryDetailOut.description:
One memory with its blast radius: the tasks it most recently shaped, newest first.
The list view stays light; the detail answers "where has this been used".
MemoryDetailOut.title: MemoryDetailOut

MessageIn.description:
One line from the owner. `start_task` is the explicit gesture (the Start-as-task
button); `reply_to_task` anchors the line on a task card (steer / follow-up).
MessageIn.title: MessageIn

ModelAddIn.description: A model to add to the catalog. **Added disabled** - enabling is a second, deliberate act.
ModelAddIn.title: ModelAddIn

ModelClass.description: What a step needs from a model, said without naming one.
ModelClass.title: ModelClass

ModelPatchIn.description:
PATCH /admin/models/{ref}: enable/disable and/or re-class, each optional, one request.

Replaced `ModelEnableIn`: "adding a model is data" implies EDITING one is too, and
`set_classes` living only as a DB-direct CLI helper made re-classing the one catalog edit
that could not ride the API. A None field is "leave it alone", never "clear it".
ModelPatchIn.title: ModelPatchIn

OkOut.description: The minimal typed acknowledgement - a write with nothing to return but its success.
OkOut.title: OkOut

PlanStepView.description: A step as the API and the CLI see it. Never an ORM row.
PlanStepView.title: PlanStepView

PoliciesIn.description:
The whole overrides map, replace semantics: what the permissions screen holds is what
the row stores. Tool names are validated against the cached inventory in operations.
PoliciesIn.title: PoliciesIn

PresenceIn.description:
A composer's typing frame. `conn` is the stream's own id (the `?conn=` the client opened
the task stream with) - validated here, so a malformed frame is a 422, never echoed.
PresenceIn.title: PresenceIn

PreviewOut.description:
The render sidecar: ONE `kind` discriminator, one payload
field per kind - sheet grids, document blocks, deck slides, code listings, or a page's own
HTML (rendered client-side in a fully sandboxed iframe; the server only carries it).
PreviewOut.title: PreviewOut

PricesIn.description:
A reprice: `{ref: {unit: usd_per_unit}}`, prices as strings so JSON never rounds a cent.
Copy-forward - name only what changes; the rest of the book carries into the new version.
PricesIn.title: PricesIn

ProjectListOut.description:
A list row. The charter (`instructions`, ≤4000 chars) rides only the detail shape -
a 200-row page of projects must not carry up to 800 KB of text no list view renders.
ProjectListOut.title: ProjectListOut

ProjectOwnerOut.description:
The owner, named. The owner is a column, never a member row, so the members
list cannot name them - and every member is owed the name of who owns the Project.
ProjectOwnerOut.title: ProjectOwnerOut

ProjectUsageOut.description:
A project's month-to-date spend against its budget. Money as strings: a Decimal must not
round-trip through a float, and the client formats currency, never arithmetics it.
ProjectUsageOut.title: ProjectUsageOut

PushDeviceIn.description: A phone registering for push: its FCM registration token and what app build holds it.
PushDeviceIn.title: PushDeviceIn

PushDeviceOut.description: A registered phone. The token never leaves the server again.
PushDeviceOut.title: PushDeviceOut

PushDevicePlatform.description: The phone a registration token belongs to.
PushDevicePlatform.title: PushDevicePlatform

QuestionSet.description: ONE numbered batch per gate - never dripped.
QuestionSet.title: QuestionSet

RemovedOut.description: A member revoked from a project - the typed answer to a DELETE (no bare dict).
RemovedOut.title: RemovedOut

ResetPasswordIn.description: The emailed `cr_…` code is the whole authentication for this request.
ResetPasswordIn.title: ResetPasswordIn

RestoreIn.description:
Restore-by-minting: the path names the revision to bring back; the body
carries the CURRENT HEAD's sha - the same optimistic-concurrency shape as revise, so two
racing restores cannot silently interleave.
RestoreIn.title: RestoreIn

RetryIn.description:
The Retry button: run the latest ask again as a new turn, whole thread in
hand. Only the duplicate-guardrail token rides along - the ask is the thread's own.
RetryIn.title: RetryIn

ReviseIn.description:
A save from the editor: the FULL next content plus the sha it was edited from.

Full content, not a patch - a collection is small, CAS dedupes unchanged bytes, and a patch
format is a merge engine nobody asked for. The content's shape pairs with the kind:
a collection sends the object; a text document (.md/.txt) sends the string -
the operation refuses the wrong pairing with the right shape named. `base_sha256` is the
optimistic-concurrency token: stale ⇒ 409 naming the newer sha, and the client rebases
its staged edits.
ReviseIn.title: ReviseIn

RoutingIn.description:
A routing table: `{capability_class: [provider:model_id, …]}`. The chains you send ARE the new
table - a class you omit falls back to alphabetical.
RoutingIn.title: RoutingIn

SaveIn.description: Save a bot's reply as a file: the format the one tap asks for.
SaveIn.title: SaveIn

ScheduleIn.description:
Exactly one of cron / every / at (the one-of law lives in schemas - operations turn its
sentence into the 422). `every` takes the duration grammar ("30m", "4h") and is checked at
this door so a typo is a 422 naming the field, never a 500; `every_s` is the resolved wire
form and either spelling is accepted. `timezone: None` ⇒ the owner's profile timezone
(operations resolves it - the serializer has no session).
ScheduleIn.title: ScheduleIn

ScreenControlIn.description:
Take control. `conn` is the tab's connection id (`CONN_PATTERN`, as every conn validator),
the one connection whose input will count; `private` turns the mask on for everyone else.
ScreenControlIn.title: ScreenControlIn

ScreenTicketIn.description:
Who asks for a screen socket: the tab's connection id (`CONN_PATTERN`, as every conn
validator) - the one the input gate compares with the lease's.
ScreenTicketIn.title: ScreenTicketIn

ScreenTicketOut.description:
A single-use `st_` ticket for `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/screen?ticket=…`, good for `expires_in`
seconds. An admission, not a credential: signed, single-use, short-lived, never stored.
ScreenTicketOut.title: ScreenTicketOut

SendOut.description:
What the door answered: the line's seq, the verdict it wore, and the task if one
started. 202 - a reply, when the verdict is `answer`, arrives on the thread.
SendOut.title: SendOut

SessionOut.description: The plaintext session token. It exists in this response and nowhere else on earth.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SessionWorkspaceIn.description: Switch the login session's active workspace - every tab on it follows.
SessionWorkspaceIn.title: SessionWorkspaceIn

SheetOut.description:
One worksheet's head, with COMPUTED values - generated in the frame by the same kind of
evaluator that verifies the workbook (harvest-time).
SheetOut.title: SheetOut

SkillCreateIn.description:
Creating a brand-new skill (POST) carries its name in the body; a push to an existing one (PUT)
takes the name from the path.
SkillCreateIn.title: SkillCreateIn

SkillFileIn.description:
One bundled file, base64 because a script or template may not be UTF-8. The
path law (scripts/ references/ assets/, no traversal) is enforced server-side in
`format.parse` - the one door - never trusted from the client.
SkillFileIn.title: SkillFileIn

SkillPushIn.description:
An author pushing an edited skill - the *raw* `SKILL.md`, `cases.yaml`, and any bundled
files, validated server-side. The client never sends a parsed manifest: the write-time
doctrine is enforced in one place (`format.parse`), so a draft that skipped the CLI and hit
the API directly obeys the same rules.
SkillPushIn.title: SkillPushIn

SpendPointOut.description: One day bucket. `key` is null (ungrouped), a `provider:model` ref, or a user email.
SpendPointOut.title: SpendPointOut

StatusOut.description: A steering action whose whole result is the task's new machine status (cancel/pause/resume).
StatusOut.title: StatusOut

command_id.description: the client's id for this command; a resend is idempotent
command_id.title: Command Id

directive.description: what to change, in plain words
directive.title: Directive

issued_epoch.description: the plan epoch the screen showed when typing began
issued_epoch.title: Issued Epoch

SteerOut.description: A steer as its author's screen tracks it: the command, the epoch it opened, its state.
SteerOut.title: SteerOut

StepState.description: The step machine. Transitions outside it raise InvalidTransition - the map is the spec.
StepState.title: StepState

StreamTicketOut.description:
A single-use `et_` ticket that opens one event stream (`GET …/events?ticket=…`) within
`expires_in` seconds. An admission, not a credential: the stream it opens re-proves the
credential that minted it, and it opens nothing else.
StreamTicketOut.title: StreamTicketOut

SuspendIn.description: Suspension takes a reason - it lands in the audit row, not the void.
SuspendIn.title: SuspendIn

TaskBudgetIn.description: The task's new USD ceiling (B3): dollars and cents, more than zero.
TaskBudgetIn.title: TaskBudgetIn

TaskCountsOut.description:
Visible-task tallies by machine status. The client folds them into its product groups -
the server counts states, it does not invent groupings.
TaskCountsOut.title: TaskCountsOut

size_marker.description:
The server-composed read-back: "extended · ~15 pages" - the ONE string
the CLI and the web chip print verbatim, so no client ever re-derives the kind's
unit. None until an `auto` resolves: the chip hides, the CLI prints nothing.
size_marker.title: Size Marker

TaskInputIn.description:
An attachment on the way in. `content` is base64 - of the **bytes**, not of the text.

Base64-in-JSON is honest for the few-megabyte documents this is for, and dishonest for a
200 MB video: it inflates by a third and it holds the whole thing in memory twice. When that
day comes the answer is a multipart upload endpoint returning a handle, and this shape becomes
`{filename, handle}` - the *schema* is already right, only the transport changes. Saying so
here is cheaper than discovering it at 3 a.m.
TaskInputIn.title: TaskInputIn

TaskInputOut.description:
An attachment as the transcript shows it - name, size, kind, and a presigned
download link (the chat's preview). The sha stays internal: provenance lives in the
verification receipt, not the chat.
TaskInputOut.title: TaskInputOut

size_marker.description:
The server-composed read-back: "extended · ~15 pages" - the ONE string
the CLI and the web chip print verbatim, so no client ever re-derives the kind's
unit. None until an `auto` resolves: the chip hides, the CLI prints nothing.
size_marker.title: Size Marker

TaskUpdateIn.description:
The user-space surface of a task: its label and its pin. The goal is immutable (it is
what was asked) and the status is the machine's - neither is editable here.
TaskUpdateIn.title: TaskUpdateIn

TemplateInstalledOut.description: One receipt + the head, for the update chip: `update_available` is computed HERE.
TemplateInstalledOut.title: TemplateInstalledOut

ToolPolicy.description:
What one tool of one connector may do. `allow` runs; `ask` pauses the step on
an approve gate the owner resolves; `off` never enters the inventory the model sees.
ToolPolicy.title: ToolPolicy

email.description: the user to transfer ownership to, by email (§6)
email.title: Email

UserApiKeyOut.description: One key, as metadata - the auth ApiKeyOut's shape, through the operator door.
UserApiKeyOut.title: UserApiKeyOut

UserSessionOut.description: One login, as metadata. Note what is absent: the token, in any form.
UserSessionOut.title: UserSessionOut

UserUpdateIn.description:
The editable slice of the profile, all optional - a PATCH sends what changed. Email is
absent deliberately: changing the login identifier is a verification flow, not a PATCH.
UserUpdateIn.title: UserUpdateIn

VerificationOut.description:
The signed report - what `prismoid artifacts verify` prints.

`signature_valid` is **recomputed at read time**, not read from a column. A stored boolean
saying "this is valid" is a boolean somebody can UPDATE; recomputing it from the canonical bytes
is the only thing an auditor could ever trust, and it is what makes the tamper test possible.
VerificationOut.title: VerificationOut

VerifierSuite.description: Named suites. Each is a pipeline in `ai/verification/` - deterministic, then judged.
VerifierSuite.title: VerifierSuite

VerifyEmailIn.description: The emailed `ev_…` code, read from the link's fragment by the page and posted here.
VerifyEmailIn.title: VerifyEmailIn

WorkspaceBriefOut.description: A workspace as its member sees it in a list or on `/v1/auth/me`.
WorkspaceBriefOut.title: WorkspaceBriefOut

info.title: Prismoid

Enable/disable and/or re-class one catalog row. `id` is the provider:model_id ref.
(Was `set_model_enabled`; grew classes with ADR-024 so every catalog edit rides the API.)

ONE transaction (validates classes before writing): the two old sequential ops could commit the
enable, then 422 on a bad class - a half-applied PATCH the client saw fail. A missing row is
`patch_model`'s own 404, so the old `assert entry is not None` (which -O strips) is gone.

post.description: Name a revision - "final draft" in the history picker; null clears.

get.description: The render sidecar - computed sheet heads for a binary artifact; 404 = none.

The full-fidelity rendition: docx/pptx as PDF, xlsx as styled HTML - and a
native `.pdf` serves its own bytes on the same inline lane (`rendition_sha256` NULL there).

post.description:
Restore-by-minting: the id names the revision to bring back; a new head
carries its bytes. Every kind, binaries included.
A human edit saved as the lineage's next immutable revision.

get.description:
The whole lineage, newest first - the version picker's list (bounded; no cursor).
Verdicts ride along (get_artifact's shape): a PASS-verified v1 must never read Pending
in the history just because a human saved a v2.

The report, and its signature **re-checked right now** (the tamper test).

A 404 here means *not verified*, which is not the same as `verdict: unverified` - the first is
"nobody has looked", the second is "we looked and could prove nothing". Conflating them is how a
system starts telling people an unchecked file is fine.

put.description:
Set a task's USD ceiling - an editor's answer to "Budget reached" (B3). Resuming is the
gate's own accept, so a client that raises and resumes makes two calls.

get.description:
`curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" "$B/v1/tasks/$ID/events?since=0"` - the flight
recorder, in a terminal. A browser, whose EventSource cannot set that header, opens it with
`?ticket=` from `POST /v1/tasks/{id}/events/ticket` instead: single-use, thirty seconds, never
the session token.

`Last-Event-ID` beats `?since=` when present. That header is the browser telling us where it
actually got to, and it is more authoritative than a query parameter written once at connect
time. Those five lines are the entire reconnect implementation.

post.description:
A single-use, thirty-second ticket for `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/events?ticket=…` (or the task's
WebSocket). Anyone who can read the task may mint one; anyone else meets the task's 404.
Continue a settled task on the same row - a new turn, same record, same stream.

Run the latest ask again as a new turn - same task, whole thread in hand.
The body is optional: a bare POST retries too (`curl -X POST …/retry`).
